title: Reds’ Elly De La Cruz will go on a rehab assignment before being activated
content:
CINCINNATI — Cincinnati Reds shortstop Elly De La Cruz could begin a minor-league rehab assignment as soon as this week if everything goes well Monday and Tuesday, when he runs on the field in front of the team’s medical staff.

The Reds’ star shortstop has been on the injured list since June 1 after suffering a strained right hamstring during a victory over the Atlanta Braves on May 31. De La Cruz has been anxious to return for at least a week, Reds manager Terry Francona said Monday, but the team doesn’t want to rush him back too soon.

“The one thing I don’t want him to ever feel is that, one, we’re not listening to him, and, two, we don’t want him to play — we’re dying for him to play,” Francona said before the Reds’ series opener against the New York Mets. “I just don’t think you can do what’s right when it’s convenient. That’s the best way. And I think down deep, I think he understands. I just think he wants to play desperately, and I respect that.”

Francona said De La Cruz could go out for a rehab assignment “this weekend,” though the team hasn’t yet determined where that will be. None of the Reds’ four full-season affiliates are at home this weekend. Double-A Chattanooga may be the closest, playing this week at Knoxville, Tenn. The Triple-A Louisville Bats might be in the most convenient spot, playing at Gwinnett (Ga.) in suburban Atlanta. High-A Dayton is at Peoria (Ill.), and Low-A Daytona is playing at Port St. Lucie (Fla.).

“Everything he’s doing — and he’s done a great job and he’s worked his ass off — but he knows where he’s going and why he’s going,” Francona said about the team’s plan to send De La Cruz on a rehab assignment before activating him. “You get into a game, and you’ve got to go in a different direction.”

The Reds are 3-9 in 12 games since De La Cruz went on the IL.

Even with De La Cruz, the Reds were 10-17 in May, beginning the month in first place in the National League Central and finishing in last, where they currently stand at 33-37.

De La Cruz’s IL stint ended a streak of 276 consecutive games played. He had started every game of the 2026 season before his injury, and he started 161 of 162 games in 2025 despite dealing with a quad injury for most of the second half of the schedule.

The Reds have lost eight of their last 10 and haven’t won a series since taking two of three from the Mets in New York last month.

Before going on the IL, De La Cruz was hitting .280/.346/.509 with 12 home runs and 10 stolen bases in 58 games.

“We need to do the right thing,” Francona said of the team’s cautious approach with De La Cruz. “Truthfully, it’s not fun doing the right thing, but it’s the right thing.”

Since De La Cruz went on the IL, the team’s regular second baseman, Matt McLain, has moved to shortstop for most of the team’s games. Entering June, McLain was hitting .196/.294/.320, but in De La Cruz’s absence, he’s gone 10-for-36 (.278), raising his season slash line to .209/.308/.365. He’s hit three of his eight home runs this month.

Rookie Edwin Arroyo, called up when De La Cruz went on the IL, made his big-league debut June 1. He has hit .214/.281/.214 in 32 plate appearances over 12 games. The switch-hitter has started six games at second base and two at shortstop.

De La Cruz was on the team’s recent road trip to St. Louis and San Diego and, upon returning to Cincinnati last week, went to a game at Dayton, about an hour’s drive from Great American Ball Park. De La Cruz didn’t work out in Dayton; he went to watch baseball.

“He doesn’t even like coming out of blowout games — I’ve taken him out of a couple of games just to get him off his feet, and he doesn’t like it,” Francona said. “He just likes to play baseball. That’s a good thing.”
